title: hyper, no framework
notes: The sample application written by hand on hyper, with hand-written routing and escaping: the cost of using no framework. Rust's standard library has no HTTP server.
details: The sample application written by hand on hyper: the cost of using no framework. Rust's standard library has no HTTP server (and no JSON), so this is not a built-in: hyper is the HTTP layer that axum and most other Rust frameworks are built on, used here directly with its HTTP/1 connection builder, a hand-written match on the path for a router, pages pushed onto a String with a hand-written escape function, and serde_json for the API. /about is one constant built on first use. Built with cargo build --release at Cargo's default optimization settings and run as one process on Tokio's default multi-threaded runtime (one worker thread per core), so idle workers cost some CPU under a light load. Cargo cannot skip build scripts or procedural macros, so those of the locked crates run at build time, as for every Rust entry here.
